 Advertisement Mass. Rep. Katherine Clark nominated to become first woman House majority leader
 Advertisement Updated: 12:28 PM EST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Veronica Haynes Senior Digital Editor/Producer, WCVB.com Mass. Rep. Katherine Clark nominated to become first woman House majority leader
 Updated: 12:28 PM EST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Veronica Haynes Senior Digital Editor/Producer, WCVB.com WASHINGTON — Rep. Katherine Clark, the House Minority Whip who has represented Massachusetts's fifth district since 2013, has been nominated to become the first woman to serve as House Majority Leader after the blue wave election propelled Democrats to control of the chamber in the next Congress.
 “It is beyond exciting,” Clark told WCVB’s "On The Record" last week about the possibility. “It is historic in that, as you said, the first woman in the 250 years of our country to hold this position, which is the second in seniority in the House of Representatives.”
 Advertisement Clark noted that the 120th Congress will also include a record 120 women in the House Democratic Caucus.
 Democrat Hakeem Jeffries is nominated to become House speaker, a historic first Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York’s 8th District also made history Wednesday when he was nominated to become the first Black speaker of the House as Democrats take control.
 “Hakeem has been a steady leader for us through the four years of minority, not afraid to take on this administration or anybody who is cheating the American people, and he has delivered a huge victory,” Clark said on "On The Record." “Hakeem played a huge role in making sure that Democrats were poised to win this House by what is a landslide.”
 Clark told "On The Record" that she, Jeffries and other party leaders are working to set priorities for the next two years. She said that includes considering priorities from the party’s progressive wing.
 Rep. Katherine Clark On The Record about Democratic leadership in Congress, investigating Jensen Huang, impeaching Pete Hegseth “With a 260-person Democratic majority, we are going to have the ability to really focus on the American people, put them back on the agenda,” Clark said.
 Clark said Americans can expect “quick action” from Democrats to reverse cuts to programs made during the first two years of President Donald Trump’s term.
 “That is what this election was about, making sure that they are not paying the price for corruption,” she said.
 Rep. Pete Aguilar of California was nominated to become the first Latino majority whip.
 Clark, Jeffries and Aguilar all ran unopposed.
